0002: Correct formula for the Hölder mean where it is defined.
0003: Correctly records the necessary domain qualification.
0004: No substantive claim; separator.
0005: Correctly invokes the definition for exponent +∞.
0006: Correct: M_∞ is the maximum.
0007: No substantive claim; separator.
0008: The cited limiting result is consistent with the definition in 0006.
0009: Correct statement of the +∞ limiting formula under the usual admissibility conditions.
0010: No substantive claim; separator.
0011: Legitimately invokes the cited maximum bound.
0012: Correct inequality wherever M_p is defined.
0013: No substantive claim; separator.
0014: Correctly signals the inference from 0006 and 0012.
0015: Correct consequence for every finite admissible exponent p.
0016: Validly closes only the preceding +∞ inequality lemma.
0017: No substantive claim; separator.
0018: Correctly invokes the definition for exponent −∞.
0019: Correct: M_{−∞} is the minimum.
0020: No substantive claim; separator.
0021: The cited limiting result is consistent with the definition in 0019.
0022: Correct statement of the −∞ limiting formula under the usual admissibility conditions.
0023: No substantive claim; separator.
0024: Legitimately invokes the cited minimum bound.
0025: Correct inequality wherever M_p is defined.
0026: No substantive claim; separator.
0027: Correctly signals the inference from 0019 and 0025.
0028: Correct consequence for every finite admissible exponent p.
0029: Validly closes only the preceding −∞ inequality lemma.
0030: No substantive claim; separator.
0031: This is a permissible setup for considering the two zero-exponent boundary cases.
0032: No substantive claim; separator.
0033: Correctly invokes the definition of the zero-exponent mean.
0034: Correct: M_0 is the geometric mean.
0035: Correctly identifies G.
0036: No substantive claim; separator.
0037: Legitimately cites the limiting characterization of M_0.
0038: Correct limiting formula under the cited result's admissibility interpretation.
0039: No substantive claim; separator.
0040: Incorrect: after handling only infinite endpoints, finite cases with p<0—including p<q<0, p<0=q, and p<0<q—still remain, so the proof cannot restrict what remains to p,q≥0.
0041: No substantive claim; separator.
0042: Not well-defined as stated: the current zero case can have p=0, making q/p undefined, and for q/p<0 the function is not defined at x=0.
0043: Invalid under the stated domain and cases because q/p may be undefined and x^{q/p} may be undefined at zero.
0044: No substantive claim; separator.
0045: The power rule is applicable only after imposing p≠0 and a suitable domain.
0046: The derivative formula is conditionally correct for p≠0 on the interior of the power function's domain.
0047: No substantive claim; separator.
0048: The cited differentiable convexity criterion is applicable only to a correctly defined function on the relevant interval.
0049: For finite p≠0 with p<q and q>0, the convexity conclusion is correct, but it is not justified for the stated p=0 case and the domain in 0042 is wrong when q/p<0.
0050: No substantive claim; separator.
0051: The cited differentiable concavity criterion is applicable only after correcting the function's parameters and domain.
0052: Conditionally correct for p<q<0, since 0<q/p<1, but it conflicts with 0040 and does not repair the undefined construction in 0042–0043.
0053: No substantive claim; separator.
0054: Jensen can be applied in the finite nonzero cases on the appropriate domain, but not as written when p=0 because φ is undefined.
0055: No substantive claim; separator.
0056: This case division is meaningful only after excluding p=0 and correcting the domain.
0057: Correct Jensen inequality for finite p≠0, p<q, q>0, with the required positivity when p<0; it does not cover the zero case currently under consideration.
0058: No substantive claim; separator.
0059: Correct reverse Jensen inequality conditionally for finite p<q<0, but that case was wrongly excluded by 0040.
0060: No substantive claim; separator.
0061: In the valid finite nonzero strict Jensen cases, equality is equivalent to all x_k being equal; as written it fails to handle p=0 and does not establish equality cases for infinite endpoints.
0062: No substantive claim; separator.
0063: Incorrect as a conclusion to the full theorem: the zero-exponent cases were never obtained by taking limits, several finite sign cases were excluded or used inconsistently, and equality for infinite endpoints was not proved.
0064: The final QED is unjustified because the failures beginning at 0040 leave the theorem incompletely proved.
